questions.question: Explain the difference between a landlocked country and a coastal country, with an example of each.
questions.expected_answer: A landlocked country has no coastline and is surrounded by other countries, for example Lesotho, Botswana or Zimbabwe. A coastal country touches the sea, for example South Africa, Namibia or Mozambique.

questions.question: Name two African countries north of the equator, two south of it, and two on it.
questions.expected_answer: North: for example Egypt and Nigeria. South: for example South Africa and Zambia. On the equator: for example Kenya and Uganda, or Gabon, the Republic of the Congo, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Somalia.

questions.question: Write two facts each about Madagascar and Zanzibar.
questions.expected_answer: Madagascar is a large island country in the Indian Ocean, off the south-east coast of Africa, with Antananarivo as its capital; it is home to lemurs and baobabs found nowhere else. Zanzibar is a group of islands off Tanzania and part of Tanzania; it is famous for spices such as cloves and for Stone Town.
